narr: A slow-moving thunderstorm developed along a stationary front stretching across Appomattox County on the afternoon of July 16th. Surface analysis just prior to the thunderstorm indicated precipitable water values in the area around 1.5 inches, while deep instability was present per surface-based CAPE in excess of 3,000 J/Kg. Steering winds were less than 5 mph. There were no rain gauges to capture ground-truth rainfall totals, however MRMS FLASH estimated portions of the Evergreen area received in excess of 5 inches of rain within a two-hour period, with up to 4 inches falling in a single hour, with rainfall rates at times exceeding 6 inches per hour. If either the 1- or 2-hour rainfall estimates is accurate, either would be close to a 1,000 year rainfall event for this area per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates. The one-hour rainfall estimate rose to one and a half times flash flood guidance in the Evergreen area, and CREST unit exceeded 600 ft^3 per second at its maximum.
ev: Rough Creek was observed well out of its banks, flowing over Old Evergreen Road at least 6 inches deep at around 3:00 pm EDT. No damage was noted to the road, which became passable again once the flooding receded.
